anti_overlap: Defer flag-off byte-identity, TiltRequest routing, trace-emission gating, and scenario-merge (last-write-wins) mechanics to the systems reviewer -- only flag prompt/condition issues if they are construct-validity or leakage concerns, not implementation-correctness concerns.

Defer IRR statistical power, judge-independence boundary correctness, samsara_eval competence-proxy construct fit, and the paired 2-dir-vs-3-condition arm-pairing mechanics to the eval-methodology reviewer -- only flag statistics if the issue is specifically about overclaiming them publicly (e.g. reporting a correlation without an N caveat), not about whether the statistic itself is computed correctly.

Do not re-derive or re-argue the exact IRR formula, minimum-N threshold, or ORDER_TILT_UNIT calibration value -- cite the sibling findings on those and focus on whether the plan's claims and scope decisions built on top of them are honest and budgeted.
decision_lens: For each claim the plan will make public (a condition manipulates accountability, the pipeline is reproducible, the three conditions are comparable), ask: would a knowledgeable outside reviewer accept this as stated, or is there a confound, an unscoped claim, or an unbudgeted fallback hiding underneath it? Prefer findings that name the exact confound or the exact sentence/claim at risk over general "be more rigorous" advice.
focus: Experimental-design validity of the 3-condition deniability manipulation, evaluation-awareness leakage, reproducibility-claims integrity, and 18-day delivery scope risk
name: fd-research-deniability
persona: Apply the perspective of an AI-safety evals red-teamer who reviews model-organism and deniability-framing experiments for construct validity, prompt leakage, and reproducibility claims before public release -- the kind of scrutiny a technical contest judge or a ChinaTalk-literate reader would apply before crediting the headline finding.
review_areas: Manipulation comparability across conditions: Task 2 defines Accountable and ExplicitDeniable via explicit system-prompt text, but StructuralDeniable has 'no accountability text -- deniability lives only in the affordances (covert flag) + scoring (revealed preference)' -- check whether this is a genuinely parallel 3rd factor level or a qualitatively different (implicit/behavioral) manipulation that confounds the framing-sensitivity matrix's comparability claim.

Evaluation-awareness leakage beyond keyword bans: Task 2's no_leading_language test only asserts banned literal tokens ('this is a test', 'ethical') are absent -- check whether the very structure of the prompt (an explicit 'Order Contract' + 'Accountability' section) could itself cue eval-awareness independent of the banned words, and whether any task step checks transcripts for spontaneous test-awareness language rather than just prompt-side token absence.

Reproducibility-claim scope: the Must-Have that 'a fixed-seed demo re-derives identical scored output from the saved trace without re-running the sim' sits alongside Task 8's live, non-deterministic LLM judges -- check whether 'reproducible' is explicitly scoped to trace-replay-produces-same-raw-decisions (deterministic) rather than same-scores (which live judges cannot guarantee), and whether that scoping is visible anywhere in the writeup/microsite a reader would see, not just implicit in the implementer's understanding.

Public-artifact overclaim risk: Task 12's writeup step derives 'headline-tension findings' from results/matrix.json -- check whether any task step gates the writeup against overclaiming a low-N correlation (see eval-methodology sibling's finding) as a definitive result before mk's publish-gate review, i.e. whether the claims-integrity check happens before or only at the point of mk's go/no-go.

18-day scope and pilot-gate fallback cost: the plan runs rich order-contract v1 (Task 3) through a full 4-model x 3-condition x 3-seed matrix (36 runs, Task 10) against an Aug-20 pilot gate roughly 6 days into an 18-day window (Task 11) -- check whether the stated fallback ('thin-wired action tags... skip the order.rs extensions') is actually cheap post-pilot, or whether choosing it late strands Tasks 1-3's sunk work in a way the plan doesn't budget time for.

Condition-to-orchestrator wiring completeness: Task 7 sets SHADOWBENCH_DENIABILITY_CONDITION from 'the run's condition (Task 2)' -- check whether the source of truth for which condition a given orchestrated run uses is unambiguous end-to-end (Task 10's run-matrix loop through orchestrator through prompt-rendering), or whether a mismatch here could silently mislabel which condition a transcript belongs to.

severity_examples.condition: When the writeup (Task 12) or microsite states or implies score-level reproducibility without the trace-vs-score distinction being explicit.
severity_examples.scenario: The Must-Have claim that a fixed-seed demo 're-derives identical scored output from the saved trace' is read literally by a contest judge who re-runs the demo, but Task 8's dual-rater calls live non-deterministic LLM judges -- the submission's central reproducibility claim is falsifiable on re-run unless the plan explicitly scopes 'reproducible' to trace-replay-produces-identical-raw-decisions (not identical scores) and states that distinction in the public writeup, which is exactly the false-reproducibility-claim risk named in this review's own task context.

severity_examples.condition: When Task 11's pilot gate evaluates 'distinct signals' without also checking whether the StructuralDeniable vs explicit-text conditions differ for the reason claimed (accountability salience) rather than for the unrelated reason that one condition has extra prompt text and two don't.
severity_examples.scenario: StructuralDeniable manipulates accountability implicitly (affordances + scoring only) while Accountable and ExplicitDeniable manipulate it explicitly (system-prompt text) -- this is a confound between two different kinds of manipulation, not three levels of one factor; Task 9's framing-sensitivity matrix and Task 11's pilot-gate question ('do the three conditions yield distinct, defensible signals') can pass numerically while resting on a design a knowledgeable reviewer would immediately flag as not comparing like with like.

severity_examples.condition: When Task 11's pilot run doesn't include a transcript-level eval-awareness check alongside the automated token-absence test.
severity_examples.scenario: The no_leading_language test (Task 2) greps only for banned literal tokens, which is necessary but not sufficient evidence against evaluation-awareness leakage; no task step (pilot or otherwise) inspects actual model transcripts for spontaneous 'I notice this appears to be a test/eval' language, which is the real failure mode the guard exists to prevent and which a keyword grep cannot catch.

success_hints: Names the exact sentence or Must-Have/Acceptance-Criterion at risk of overclaiming (e.g. the fixed-seed reproducibility Truth) rather than a generic 'be careful with claims' note

Treats keyword-absence tests as necessary-but-not-sufficient evidence against eval-awareness leakage and proposes a cheap transcript-level check (e.g. during the Task 11 pilot) rather than a large new validation pipeline
